output.name: Mesul — The Ferry That Never Lands
output.myth: Grandmothers say the Mesul is a ferry with one sail and no oars. Ennu cut its cloth from the sail of the first drowned man, and Hesk knotted its mast to the string she winds at the pole. When a boat goes down in the Leeward sea, the drowned stand up and look for the stern lamp. The grey gull that lost a word watches from the north-west and carries their names up, one word short. South-east, Lavesk the Drying Shag stands where the men went under, and their wives still set the kettle on. The ferry comes, takes them aboard, and asks one question: did you fly your kite well? Say yes and she hands you a line to hold. Kael has cast for the ferry since there was water and never caught it, which is why it still runs. It sails out across the dark and never touches the far shore. Sil calls Aun's name when she sees the sail go by, but the ferry does not stop. Keep a lamp in your window for your drowned. That is all the ferry asks.
output.finding: From the Gull Who Lost a Word, look a fist and a third to the south-east, and the Mesul sails low in the Leeward sky.
